findings.evidence: grep `namespace Bilin` → only Kinematics/Basic.lean:31 (added by this PR) and Tensors/Basic.lean:94; the latter sits inside `namespace Tensors` (lines 84-88), so its full name is `...Tensors.Bilin`.
findings.fix: Keep one `Bilin` namespace. Since the `Bilin` abbrev is defined in `Kinematics`, change Tensors/Basic.lean:94 to `namespace Kinematics.Bilin` (call sites still resolve via `open Kinematics (Bilin)`), or declare the new lemma in the existing `Bilin` block in Tensors/Basic.lean.
findings.issue: `namespace Bilin` here creates `...DIS.Kinematics.Bilin`, while every other `Bilin` lemma (`reflect`, `reflect_apply_self`, `reflect_isometry`, and the new `det_reflect`) lives in the pre-existing `...DIS.Tensors.Bilin` (Tensors/Basic.lean:94). Two namespaces with the same leaf name now hold lemmas about the same abbrev: in ParityOdd.lean `Bilin.apply_eq_zero_of_apply_eq_self_of_apply_eq_neg` (line 158) and in Basic.lean `Bilin.reflect_apply_self` (line 1032) resolve to different namespaces with no visible difference, and any future duplicate leaf name makes `Bilin.*` ambiguous.

findings.evidence: Line 384 `noncomputable def aFour (K : DisKinematics (Fin 4 → ℝ))`; lines 395/445/449/454/487 all fix `K := kFour`; the file's own section docstring (lines 339-341) states that only `aFour` and `parityOddAssumptions_aFour` are general and "the remaining declarations of this section are specialized to the witness".
findings.fix: Name the instance in the specialized declarations: `aFour_kFour_apply`, `aFour_kFour_ne_zero`, `aFour_kFour_e₁_e₂`, `existsUnique_eq_smul_aFour_kFour`, `not_isLorentzCovariant_aFour_kFour` — matching the sibling `spectatorPartners_kFour` and `pTransverse_kFour`, which do name the instance.
findings.issue: `aFour` is a family indexed by `K` (line 384), but lemmas named after it state only the `kFour` instance, so the names claim more than the statements. `aFour_ne_zero : aFour kFour ≠ 0` reads as a property of `aFour`, yet `aFour K = 0` whenever `K.p`, `K.q` are dependent; `aFour_apply` (line 395) is a general-sounding `@[simp]` `_apply` lemma that only fires on `aFour kFour`. Same mismatch in `aFour_e₁_e₂` (445), `existsUnique_eq_smul_aFour` (454) and `not_isLorentzCovariant_aFour` (487), while the genuinely general lemma is `parityOddAssumptions_aFour` (414).

findings.evidence: Both declarations take a `SpectatorPlane g K` and return a structure (`SpectatorSplitting g K`, `SpectatorPartners g K`); line 1126 uses the real parent projection name `toSpectatorSplitting` in the same `where` block.
findings.fix: Rename to `SpectatorPlane.toSpectatorPartners`, matching the adjacent `toSpectatorSplitting` and the `Foo.toBar` convention for structure conversions.
findings.issue: Two conversions out of `SpectatorPlane` added in the same PR use different naming schemes: `SpectatorPlane.toSpectatorSplitting` (line 1112) and `SpectatorPlane.spectatorPartners` (line 1122). A consumer holding `hP : SpectatorPlane g K` cannot guess that `hP.toSpectatorPartners` does not exist.

summary: Names mostly describe their conclusions in standard terminology (`IsProperLorentzCovariant`, `existsUnique_sub_flip_eq_smul`, `det_reflect`) and no notation is introduced, but the PR creates a second `Bilin` namespace with the same leaf name as the existing one, and several `Witness` lemmas are named after the family `aFour` while stating facts only about `aFour kFour`.
